intro: Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.q: Set passage task in the portal response box (6 marks, our own question): 'Explain what Qur'an 2:183-185 teaches about fasting.' Frame: three points, each developed with a quote and an explanation. Start: 'Firstly, 2:183 teaches that ...'
questions.a: Taqwa as the purpose (2:183); concessions for the ill and travellers and fidyah (2:184); Ramadan linked to the Qur'an and Allah's wish for ease (2:185), each explained
questions.model: Teacher writes point 1: 'Firstly, 2:183 teaches that fasting is prescribed so that Muslims attain taqwa. This means fasting trains a Muslim to obey Allah even when no one is watching.'

questions.a: Fasting was prescribed to earlier communities too, so it is part of the shared message of the prophets

questions.q: Describe the nature of fasting in Ramadan. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Abstaining from food, drink and marital relations from true dawn to sunset; with intention; for the whole month of Ramadan; with suhur and iftar.
questions.model: One mark per accurate point: 1) no food, drink or marital relations; 2) from true dawn to sunset; 3) intention each night; 4) the whole month, which begins with the new moon.

questions.q: 2:185 says Ramadan is the month in which ...

Case studies on the pupil PDF: six people (a diabetic who must eat regularly; a pilot flying long-haul; a ten-year-old; a grandfather of 90; a student with exams; a nurse on night shifts). For each: exempt or not, what they do, and the evidence. Then a 6-mark answer in the portal response box: 'Explain why some Muslims are exempt from fasting.'
questions.a: Diabetic: exempt if medical advice says so, fidyah if permanent; pilot: traveller, may make up; child: not required; grandfather: fidyah; student: not exempt; nurse: not exempt unless harm; 6-mark with 2:184-185 and 2:286
questions.model: Teacher does the grandfather: 'Exempt: he cannot fast and will not be able to make up. He pays fidyah, feeding a poor person for each day (2:184).'

questions.q: why do scholars differ about pregnant and breastfeeding women?
questions.a: The texts can be read as qada', fidyah, or both, depending on whether the fear is for the mother or the child

questions.q: Explain the difference between qada' and fidyah. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: Qada' is making up the missed days later, for temporary reasons (illness, travel); fidyah is feeding a poor person for each day, for those who can never fast (elderly, permanent illness), from 2:184.
questions.model: Point 1: qada'. Develop: for temporary reasons like travel, the days are fasted later (2:184). Point 2: fidyah. Develop: for permanent inability, a poor person is fed for each day (2:184).

Set passage task in the portal response box (6 marks, our own question): 'Explain what Qur'an 9:58-60 teaches about zakah.' Three developed points. Start: 'Firstly, 9:60 teaches that ...'
questions.a: Eight named recipients (9:60); an obligation from Allah, not a favour (9:60); criticism of those who judged the distribution by their own gain (9:58-59), each explained
questions.model: Teacher writes point 1: 'Firstly, 9:60 teaches that zakah may only go to eight groups, beginning with the poor and the needy. This means a Muslim cannot simply give zakah to whoever he likes.'

questions.q: a worked example: Amina has £10,000 savings held for a year, above the nisab. How much zakah?
